comparison: Both evaluations agree that the extract system characterization and spindle size measurements are well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative measurements (C34, C35, C39, C40) and morphological observations. Peer reviewers explicitly praise this 'first part of the paper' as 'profound and very important.' High concordance with 11 shared claims (C2, C28-C35, C39, C40).

Both agree that cytoplasmic control of spindle size is demonstrated. OpenEval cites dose-dependent mixing experiments and nuclear independence (C41-C45). Peer reviewers include these claims in the 'profound and very important' first part. All 5 claims overlap (C41-C45).

Perfect agreement on MT nucleation pathway differences between developmental stages. Both evaluations accept the observational evidence (C46-C49) and RanT24N validation (C50-C51). Complete overlap of all 6 claims with no concerns raised by either evaluation.

Strong agreement on MT dynamics measurements. Both accept the threefold increase in catastrophe frequency (C52) and other parameter measurements (C54-C58). OpenEval includes computational validation (C53) not explicitly mentioned by peer reviewers. 7 of 8 claims overlap.

Both agree on kif2a's role as a driver of spindle size differences. OpenEval finds immunofluorescence, immunoblotting, and inhibition experiments sufficient (C60-C65). Peer reviewers accept kif2a identification but note concerns about mechanistic depth in the broader context. 6 claims overlap (C60-C65), with peer review also including C3.

Disagreement on importin α regulation of kif2a. OpenEval finds sequence analysis (C68), biochemical interaction (C69), and functional validation (C71) sufficient. Peer reviewers find the mechanistic evidence insufficient, requesting more direct quantitative measurements (FCS, FRET, quantitative pull-downs). 3 claims overlap (C68, C69, C71).

Disagreement on the kif2a-importin α regulatory mechanism. OpenEval finds reciprocal manipulations and dose-dependent effects (C72-C76) provide strong evidence. Peer reviewers consider the overall importin α mechanism insufficiently demonstrated, requesting more quantitative data. All 5 claims overlap (C72-C76).

Major disagreement on importin α redistribution mechanism. OpenEval finds biochemical fractionation, immunofluorescence, and pull-down experiments sufficient (C66-C84). Peer reviewers explicitly state this needs 'more direct and quantitative' demonstration, requesting FCS, FRET, or quantitative pull-downs. 9 claims overlap (C66, C77-C84), with peer review also including C102-C103.

Agreement on in vivo validation of spindle size effects on orientation. Both accept microinjection experiments and quantitative measurements (C6, C87-C90). OpenEval also includes chromosome segregation robustness (C91-C93) not in this peer result. 5 claims overlap (C6, C87-C90), with C120 also shared.

Agreement on chromosome segregation robustness despite spindle size changes. Both accept observations that segregation remains accurate (C7, C91-C93). 4 claims overlap with no concerns raised by either evaluation.

Partial disagreement on integrative conclusions. OpenEval finds the overall mechanism well-supported by prior results. Peer reviewers accept the work as 'worth publishing' but indicate mechanistic insights are not extensive enough, particularly regarding importin α redistribution. 3 claims overlap (C8, C104, C105).

Disagreement on the ratiometric mechanism and importin α redistribution (C102, C103). OpenEval considers membrane partitioning data sufficient for the inference. Peer reviewers find this core mechanistic claim insufficiently quantified. 2 claims overlap (C102, C103).

Divergent assessments of orientation mechanism. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the frictional resistance explanation (C98-C99) is speculative. Peer reviewers accept the orientation findings (C89-C90, C120) without questioning the mechanism. Only C120 overlaps.

Both acknowledge incomplete mechanisms. OpenEval finds the integration with prior work on MT destabilization (C100) and acknowledgment of incompleteness (C106) appropriately supported. Peer reviewers' uncertainty about overall mechanistic completeness aligns with C106 but extends to the broader model. 2 claims overlap (C100, C106).

OpenEval evaluates the integrative role of importin α in coordinating nuclear and spindle size (C108-C110) as UNCERTAIN, noting the coordination hypothesis is speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval finds the novelty claim about importin α regulation of MT-destabilizing proteins (C111) supported by experimental demonstration and absence of prior reports. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific novelty claim.

OpenEval rates the frictional resistance mechanism for orientation (C96-C99) as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature. While peer reviewers accept orientation findings (in R7), they don't specifically evaluate the mechanistic explanation that OpenEval questions.
